concepts.def: The Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Planets orbit the Sun in ellipses.
Gravity provides the centripetal force for orbits.
Icy bodies on highly elliptical orbits.
Rocky bodies, mostly between Mars and Jupiter.
Bodies like Pluto that don't clear their orbit.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Exploring the Solar System — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exploring the Solar System brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exploring the Solar System.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a terrestrial planet?
options: Jupiter
Mars
Saturn
Neptune
It is on fire
Ice sublimates near the Sun, releasing gas and dust
It collides with asteroids
Of magnetic fields only

mcqs.q: The asteroid belt lies mainly between:
options: Earth and Mars
Mars and Jupiter
Jupiter and Saturn
Neptune and the Kuiper Belt

mcqs.q: Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet because it:
options: Is too cold
Has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood
Has no moons
Is made of gas
No - since 2006 it is a dwarf planet, because it has not cleared its orbit.
Because it is closest to the Sun.
Yes, it is the ninth planet.
It is an asteroid.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an asteroid and a comet?
options: Asteroids are rocky or metallic; comets are icy and grow tails near the Sun.
Comets are rocky and asteroids are icy.
They are the same kind of object.
It is an asteroid.

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter called a gas giant?
options: Because it is the hottest planet.
Comets are rocky and asteroids are icy.
It is huge and made mostly of hydrogen and helium with no solid surface.
Because it is closest to the Sun.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Kuiper Belt”?
options: A large, low-density gas or ice giant of the outer Solar System - Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune - with thick atmospheres and ring systems.
A ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit, including dwarf planets such as Pluto, thought to be a source of short-period comets.
A rocky or metallic body, mostly orbiting the Sun in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, far smaller than a planet.
A small, dense, rocky planet of the inner Solar System - Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars - with a solid surface and few or no moons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Asteroid”?
options: A small, dense, rocky planet of the inner Solar System - Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars - with a solid surface and few or no moons.
A body orbiting the Sun that is rounded by its own gravity but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood, such as Pluto, Eris and Ceres.
A rocky or metallic body, mostly orbiting the Sun in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, far smaller than a planet.
A ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit, including dwarf planets such as Pluto, thought to be a source of short-period comets.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Comet”?
options: A rocky or metallic body, mostly orbiting the Sun in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, far smaller than a planet.
An icy body that develops a glowing coma and tails of gas and dust when its orbit brings it close enough to the Sun for the ice to sublimate.
A small, dense, rocky planet of the inner Solar System - Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars - with a solid surface and few or no moons.
A ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit, including dwarf planets such as Pluto, thought to be a source of short-period comets.

An icy body that develops a glowing coma and tails of gas and dust when its orbit brings it close enough to the Sun for the ice to sublimate.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Terrestrial planet”?
options: A ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit, including dwarf planets such as Pluto, thought to be a source of short-period comets.

A body orbiting the Sun that is rounded by its own gravity but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood, such as Pluto, Eris and Ceres.

options: A small, dense, rocky planet of the inner Solar System - Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars - with a solid surface and few or no moons.
A body orbiting the Sun that is rounded by its own gravity but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood, such as Pluto, Eris and Ceres.
A rocky or metallic body, mostly orbiting the Sun in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, far smaller than a planet.
